blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: Some families have maids.
exercises.why: **В** and **на** can also call the accusative case to refer to the direction towards which something is moving into or onto ('I'm walking *into* Moscow', 'He climbed *onto* the roof'). As a memory aid, recall that when **в** and **на** refer to the *location* of something, they use the prepositional case, which was once called the *locative* case. **О/об/обо** calls the accusative to mean 'against' or 'upon' something ('He leant upon the wall'). — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0). From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 16.  ·  «The prepositional case is always used with a preposition. With the prepositions в and на it denotes a location … With the preposition о, об this case answers the questions о ком? о чём?» — DLI, Lesson 16.
exercises.context: В** and **на can also call the accusative case to refer to the direction towards which something is moving into or onto ('I'm walking *into* Moscow', 'He climbed *onto* the roof').

exercises.q: Мне дают дополнительное время на ___ (экзамены), потому что я дислексик.
exercises.prompt: I get extra time on exams because I'm dyslexic.
exercises.why: Они на экзамене.* With the preposition **о**, **об**† this case answers the questions: **О ком?** (About whom?) *Мы говорим о студенте.* **О чём?** (About what?) *Мы говорим о классе.* The basic ending of the prepositional case singular is **-е**.* — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0). From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lesson 16.  ·  «The prepositional case is always used with a preposition. With the prepositions в and на it denotes a location … With the preposition о, об this case answers the questions о ком? о чём?» — DLI, Lesson 16.
exercises.context: Они на экзамене.
